accepted.s: Which of the following findings is associated with the Srikrishna Commission's inquiry into the Mumbai riots?
o: The riots resulted solely from economic competition
The police administration had no role in the riots
Administrative failure was a contributing cause
The riots were caused exclusively by foreign interference
accepted.x: The Srikrishna Commission identified administrative failure as one of the causes of the Mumbai riots.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific commission finding rather than attributing the event to a broader general cause.
accepted.sec: Role of police and administration - Sachar Committee, police reforms

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of the police during communal violence:
1. During Partition, the police were either complicit or helpless in different situations.
2. Police inaction and biased intelligence have been identified as factors aggravating communal violence.
3. Administrative failure has no relevance to the occurrence of communal riots.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because administrative failure itself can be a cause of communal violence.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the established relationship between administrative failure and communal violence.
accepted.sec: Role of police and administration - Sachar Committee, police reforms

accepted.s: The Sachar Committee, constituted in 2005, highlighted which of the following conditions relating to Muslims in India?
o: Higher educational attainment than all other communities
Equal representation in the police and other public services
Over-representation in all categories of public employment
Lagging educational and employment status with under-representation in public employment
accepted.x: The Sachar Committee found that Muslims lagged in education and employment and were under-represented in public employment, including the police.
accepted.tq: Use the committee's central finding and distinguish under-representation from its opposite.
accepted.sec: Role of police and administration - Sachar Committee, police reforms

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT mandated as part of the police reforms in Prakash Singh v. Union of India (2006)?
o: A single authority exclusively controlling all criminal trials
accepted.x: The judgment mandated bodies such as the State Security Commission, Police Establishment Board and Police Complaints Authority, along with separation of investigation from law and order. It did not create an authority controlling all criminal trials.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the cluster of police-reform institutions.
accepted.sec: Role of police and administration - Sachar Committee, police reforms

accepted.s: In Prakash Singh v. Union of India (2006), which structural separation was directed in police functioning?
o: Separation of intelligence from all policing functions
Separation of police from the criminal justice system
Separation of the State Security Commission from the police department
Separation of investigation from law and order
accepted.x: One of the police-reform directions was to separate investigation from law-and-order functions.
accepted.tq: Test the exact institutional separation rather than a broad description of police autonomy.
accepted.sec: Role of police and administration - Sachar Committee, police reforms

accepted.s: The direction to appoint nodal officers in every district to prevent mob violence and hate crimes was given in which case?
o: Ramji Lal Modi v. State of Uttar Pradesh
Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan v. Union of India
Tehseen Poonawalla v. Union of India
Prakash Singh v. Union of India
accepted.x: In Tehseen Poonawalla (2018), the Supreme Court directed the appointment of nodal officers in every district to prevent mob violence and hate crimes.
accepted.tq: Match the preventive direction with the correct case name and year.
accepted.sec: Role of police and administration - Sachar Committee, police reforms

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
 a. Prakash Singh v. Union of India
 b. Tehseen Poonawalla
 c. Ramji Lal Modi v. State of Uttar Pradesh
 d. Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan v. Union of India

List-II (Associated subject)
 i. Validity of Section 295A
 ii. Police reforms
 iii. Direction concerning hate-speech definition
 iv. Nodal officers for mob violence and hate crimes

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Prakash Singh is associated with police reforms; Tehseen Poonawalla with nodal officers; Ramji Lal Modi with Section 295A; and Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan with the request to define hate speech.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure case-subject pairs and eliminate codes containing swapped judicial issues.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about hate speech in India is correct?
o: It is not specifically defined in Indian law
It is defined exclusively by the Supreme Court
It is specifically and comprehensively defined in the Constitution
It is defined only in the Indian Penal Code and nowhere else
accepted.x: Hate speech is not specifically defined in Indian law.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the absence of a specific statutory definition from the existence of provisions that regulate related conduct.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: The Law Commission's 267th Report, submitted in 2017, recommended that hate speech should be defined primarily on the basis of:
o: The popularity of the speech among listeners
The speaker's political affiliation and social status
The location in which the speech was delivered
Incitement and targeting that cause or threaten harm
accepted.x: The 267th Law Commission Report recommended harm-based definitions centred on incitement and targeting.
accepted.tq: Identify the conceptual basis of the recommendation rather than an irrelevant attribute of the speaker or venue.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: In which case did the Supreme Court ask the Law Commission to define hate speech?
o: Ramji Lal Modi v. State of Uttar Pradesh
Tehseen Poonawalla v. Union of India
Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan v. Union of India
Prakash Singh v. Union of India
accepted.x: In Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan v. Union of India (2014), the Supreme Court asked the Law Commission to define hate speech.
accepted.tq: Separate the case concerning a request for a hate-speech definition from cases concerning police reform or Section 295A.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of Section 295A of the IPC in:
o: Tehseen Poonawalla v. Union of India
Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan v. Union of India
Ramji Lal Modi v. State of Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: Ramji Lal Modi v. State of Uttar Pradesh upheld Section 295A of the Indian Penal Code.
accepted.tq: Associate the constitutional validity ruling with the correct case rather than the case dealing with hate-speech definition.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s:
Match the offence with the corresponding provision under the Indian Penal Code and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:

List-I (Offence)
 a. Promoting enmity between groups
 b. Deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings
 c. Statements conducing to public mischief

List-II (Provisions)
 i. IPC 295A; BNS 299
 ii. IPC 505; BNS 353
 iii. IPC 153A; BNS 196

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Promoting enmity is covered by IPC Section 153A and BNS Section 196; deliberate acts outraging religious feelings by IPC Section 295A and BNS Section 299; and statements conducing to public mischief by IPC Section 505 and BNS Section 353.
accepted.tq: Begin with the exact section-number pairs and reject options that interchange the offences.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, promoting enmity between groups on grounds such as religion, race or language is associated with:
accepted.x: BNS Section 196 corresponds to the offence of promoting enmity between groups; the related IPC provision was Section 153A.
accepted.tq: Use the old-law and new-law correspondence to avoid swapping neighbouring BNS section numbers.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings are covered by:
accepted.x: BNS Section 299 corresponds to IPC Section 295A concerning deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the BNS provisions by matching the offence, not merely the section number.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the reported conviction rate under Section 153A of the IPC?
accepted.x: The reported conviction rate under Section 153A was 20.2%.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact percentage and reject distractors formed by changing the leading digit.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: Hate-speech cases reportedly rose by what percentage between 2014 and 2020?
accepted.x: Hate-speech cases were reported to have increased by 500% between 2014 and 2020.
accepted.tq: Test the precise trend figure rather than the general statement that cases increased.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: FIRs relating to communal or hate-speech offences were reported to rise by approximately what range before elections?
accepted.x: The reported increase in FIRs before elections was in the range of 30% to 50%.
accepted.tq: Use the range carefully; the middle values are not interchangeable with the reported election-period increase.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025:
1. It was described as the first State-level law to define hate speech.
2. It provides for imprisonment ranging from two to ten years.
3. It excludes organisations from liability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Bill provides for organisational liability.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed liability provision in an otherwise accurate description of the Bill.
accepted.sec: Hate speech and communal violence - Law Commission reports, IPC/BNS provisions

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the history of communal incidents in Hyderabad's old city?
o: 1978 — disturbances after the Rameeza Bee case
2007 — beginning of construction of Mecca Masjid
accepted.x: Hyderabad's old city witnessed notable riots in 1978 after the Rameeza Bee case. Telangana was formed in 2014, Mecca Masjid was completed in 1693, and its blast occurred in 2007.
accepted.tq: Check the event-year pairing and reject options that attach unrelated historical events to the date.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - communal incidents and peace-building (Hyderabad old city history)

accepted.s: The Mecca Masjid blast of 18 May 2007 was followed by:
o: The completion of the mosque by Aurangzeb
accepted.x: The Mecca Masjid blast on 18 May 2007 was followed by tension and police firing.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate consequence associated with the dated event.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - communal incidents and peace-building (Hyderabad old city history)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Completion of Mecca Masjid by Aurangzeb
B. Riots in Hyderabad's old city after the Rameeza Bee case
C. Riots in Hyderabad's old city in 1990
D. Mecca Masjid blast
accepted.x: Mecca Masjid was completed in 1693, the Rameeza Bee-related disturbances occurred in 1978, old-city riots occurred again in 1990, and the blast took place in 2007.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest construction date first and then arrange the twentieth- and twenty-first-century incidents.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - communal incidents and peace-building (Hyderabad old city history)

accepted.s: Who began the construction of Mecca Masjid in Hyderabad in 1614?
accepted.x: Construction of Mecca Masjid was begun by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1614.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the initiator of construction from the ruler associated with its later completion.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - communal incidents and peace-building (Hyderabad old city history)

accepted.s: Mecca Masjid was completed in 1693 by:
accepted.x: Mecca Masjid was completed by Aurangzeb in 1693, after its construction had been begun by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1614.
accepted.tq: Separate the person who began construction from the person who completed it.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - communal incidents and peace-building (Hyderabad old city history)

accepted.s: Hyderabad has been part of Telangana since:
accepted.x: Hyderabad has been in Telangana since the formation of the State in 2014.
accepted.tq: Use the State-reorganisation date and reject dates belonging to unrelated incidents or later statistics.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - communal incidents and peace-building (Hyderabad old city history)

accepted.s: According to the AP Home Department's annual note, riots in present-day Andhra Pradesh fell by what percentage in 2025?
accepted.x: The AP Home Department's annual note reported a 53.88% decline in riots in 2025.
accepted.tq: Test the exact percentage rather than the direction of change alone.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - communal incidents and peace-building (Hyderabad old city history)

accepted.s: Which of the following developments was reported in relation to a 2013 riot case in a Muzaffarnagar court?
o: Withdrawal was allowed against 25 people, including former Union Minister Sanjeev Balyan
The case was transferred to the Supreme Court for constitutional review
A new State-level hate-speech law was enacted
All accused were convicted without trial
accepted.x: A Muzaffarnagar court allowed withdrawal of a 2013 riot case against 25 people, including former Union Minister Sanjeev Balyan.
accepted.tq: Match the court action, number of persons and named public figure in the reported development.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Thirty-seven accused in a communal-riot case were reportedly acquitted because of:
o: A finding that communal violence is not an offence
Automatic withdrawal of every communal case
accepted.x: The 37 accused were acquitted for lack of proof.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated legal basis for acquittal and reject extreme generalisations about communal cases.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a consequence of low conviction rates and withdrawal of cases in communal-violence matters?
accepted.x: Low conviction rates and case withdrawals are criticised for weakening deterrence against communal violence.
accepted.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect relationship between enforcement outcomes and deterrence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The draft communal violence law has been criticised in public debate primarily on the ground that it is:
accepted.x: The draft communal violence law has been attacked as one-sided.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific criticism rather than substituting an unrelated objection.
